record.title: A paper models GPU energy per output token from active bytes and decode time
record.summary: A new arXiv paper proposes a compact model for GPU-board energy per output token during dense, full-history LLM decoding. The model combines logical weight and KV-cache bytes per output with observed decode time, using coefficients calibrated separately for each model and hardware/runtime configuration. Across three BF16 models on GH200 and GB300 GPUs, plus a two-GH200 tensor-parallel setup, the authors report held-out condition-mean estimates within 3.73% of measured board energy across 270 executions and 54 static conditions. In the tested ranges, larger batches use less mean board energy per useful output, while longer histories increase it. These author-reported fits are configuration-specific; independent reproduction, facility energy and monetary savings are not established.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors propose a GPU-board energy-per-output-token model for dense, full-history decoding. It combines logical dense-weight bytes amortized across the realized batch, per-request KV-history bytes, and observed decode time; fitted coefficients are specific to each model and hardware/runtime configuration.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For BF16 decoding of Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-14B and Mistral-7B on NVIDIA GH200 and GB300, plus a two-GH200 tensor-parallel Qwen2.5-7B setup, the authors report held-out condition-mean energy estimates within 3.73% of measurement across 270 executions and 54 static-workload conditions. The device-transfer condition retains source-device coefficients.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across six single-GPU model/platform pairs in the paper’s tested range, the largest tested batch has 33.2–46.8% lower measured mean GPU-board energy per useful output than the smallest tested batch at matched model and history; measured mean energy rises with longer tested histories at fixed batch.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The paper studies dense full-history BF16 decode on three models and NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell GPUs. Its coefficients are calibrated per model/platform/runtime, energy is measured at the GPU-board boundary, and the paper does not establish facility energy or monetary cost.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: No independent reproduction, portable coefficient set, facility-level energy result, or general serving-cost reduction is established by this paper-level review.

evidence_gaps.description: The model’s reported coefficients and held-out predictions have not been independently reproduced; the observed 3.73% maximum is across author-selected condition means and configurations.
Measured boundary is GPU-board energy, and the model covers dense full-history BF16 decode rather than prefill, facility overhead, or every serving architecture.
No author-linked measurement scripts or raw energy traces surfaced in the bounded artifact search.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported relationship generalizes within comparable dense-decoding deployments, estimating GPU-board energy as batch and context change could improve inference efficiency comparisons and operating decisions. The consequence is meaningful at serving scale, while validation remains local to three models and a small Hopper/Blackwell configuration set and does not establish facility-wide savings.
limitations: The paper’s results are author-reported and have not been independently reproduced.
The model predicts GPU-board energy for dense full-history BF16 decoding; it does not measure facility energy, prefill, or end-to-end monetary costs.
Energy-model coefficients are calibrated per model and hardware/runtime configuration and must not be treated as universal or portable without validation.
The evaluation includes three models on GH200 and GB300 plus a two-GH200 tensor-parallel configuration; broader architectures, workloads and hardware are untested.
Reported held-out error compares condition means in the authors’ design; it does not establish out-of-domain predictive accuracy or production savings.
No author-linked reproducibility artifact or independent reproduction was located in this bounded review; search absence does not prove no artifact exists.
brief.summary: A new arXiv paper proposes a compact model for GPU-board energy per output token during dense, full-history LLM decoding. The model combines logical weight and KV-cache bytes per output with observed decode time, using coefficients calibrated separately for each model and hardware/runtime configuration. Across three BF16 models on GH200 and GB300 GPUs, plus a two-GH200 tensor-parallel setup, the authors report held-out condition-mean estimates within 3.73% of measured board energy across 270 executions and 54 static conditions. In the tested ranges, larger batches use less mean board energy per useful output, while longer histories increase it. These author-reported fits are configuration-specific; independent reproduction, facility energy and monetary savings are not established.

technical.claimed_result: Held-out condition-mean model estimates are within 3.73% of measured GPU-board energy per useful output across 270 executions and 54 static conditions for three BF16 models on GH200/GB300 and two-GPU GH200. In six single-GPU model-platform pairs, the authors report 33.2–46.8% lower measured mean board energy at the largest versus smallest tested batch, and higher energy at longer histories for fixed batch.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary preprint documents the proposed active-byte/work–time model, measurement protocol and author-reported validation. the research desk has not reproduced the measurements or validated portability.
technical.mechanism: The model estimates per-output-token GPU-board energy as an affine response to dense weight bytes amortized across realized batch size, private KV-history bytes per output, and elapsed decode time per useful output token. Coefficients are fitted for each model and hardware/runtime stratum.
technical.regime: Dense full-history BF16 decoding for Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-14B and Mistral-7B on NVIDIA GH200 and GB300, with one two-GH200 tensor-parallel Qwen2.5-7B setup. Evaluation reports held-out condition means and repeated runs; coefficient portability beyond tested configurations is not established.
technical.reproducibility: The paper reports 270 executions across 54 static-workload conditions and a separate same-SKU device transfer; this activation reviewed the full paper sections and tables but did not execute code. A bounded exact-title/arXiv-ID artifact search did not locate author-linked scripts or raw traces; their absence is not established.
technical.strongest_baseline: Within each listed model/platform, the paper compares measured board energy across batch and history settings and validates model predictions on held-out conditions. These within-study results do not compare providers, model quality, facility energy, or total serving costs.

brief.title: A paper models GPU energy per output token from active bytes and decode time
brief.why_it_matters: Batch size and context length jointly shape inference energy, but token counts alone do not describe the work or time spent generating each output. If independently reproduced within real serving regimes, this model could make hardware and batching efficiency comparisons more informative. Its present evidence is a configuration-specific, author-run GPU-board study, not a general energy or cost forecast.
